notes: Swimlane walk of the SIPOC's register-to-handoff segment, first drawn July 21, step times filled in August 3 from the time study's element medians (typical cycle, robust to the flagged July 28 rush outlier): 0.8 + 4.5 + 2.0 + 0.6 + 0.5 = 8.4 minutes -- the charter baseline. Demand block: espresso station staffed 6:30-10:30 (240 min) around the peak; 48 espresso orders per peak (July tally, same count the spaghetti observation logged) -- pace 5.0 min per order, the same five minutes the customer named as the walk-away line (VoC S4). The engine names the drink-queue wait as the constraint: the wait is the bottleneck, not the work.

steps.name: Take order and payment at register
steps.reason: Order and payment must be captured, but the customer is buying the drink, not the transaction

steps.name: Cup waits in drink queue
steps.reason: Pure queue time -- nothing happens to the drink; more than half of the 8.4-minute total

wastes.note: Cups sit a median 4.5 min untouched (time study el-queue) -- the largest single block of the order-to-handoff total
Marked cups are WIP between register and machine -- nine deep during the July 28 8:12 rush

steps.name: Prepare drink at espresso station
steps.reason: The transformation the customer pays for: dose, pull, steam, build

wastes.note: Grinder rework: 10 of the 40 tallied delays were re-pulls after sour or channelled shots (check sheet)
A grinder round trip per drink -- the grinder sits 2.3 m from the machine at the far end of the back counter (spaghetti route R2, 52 trips per peak)

steps.name: Finish drink (syrup, lid, sleeve)
steps.reason: Completes the sellable drink -- the syrup, lid, and sleeve the customer ordered

steps.name: Call name and hand off at pickup counter
steps.reason: Required delivery moment, no transformation -- SIPOC steps 5-6, timed as one element in the study

wastes.note: Finished drinks sit while the name call waits for a gap -- VoC S3: 'nobody called my name'
